words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may prevent wrongdoing by blocking its means or requiring precaution; burdens imposed as punishment for a person's prior bad choice are not intrinsically impossible obligations.
rows.anchor: فمن الممكن أن يمنع عنهما مانع بالمنع عن مقدماتهما أو بإيجاب التحفظ عنهما

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ خَطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their unqualified assent, the believers acknowledge their weakness and the fate of earlier peoples, asking for mercy because they have no power or protection apart from God.
rows.anchor: لما قالوا في مقام إجابة الدعوة سمعنا وأطعنا، وهو قول ينبئ عن الإجابة المطلقة من غير تقييد

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ خَطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Prophet is protected from error and forgetfulness, he relies on God's protection and may ask for what he cannot secure from himself, joining the community of believers.
rows.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وإن كان معصوما من الخطأ والنسيان لكنه إنما يعتصم بعصمة الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported definition of الإصر is a heavy burden.
rows.anchor: الإصر هو الثقل على ما قيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported definition is forcibly confining something; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this is close to burden, since confinement imposes what is disliked and heavy.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو حبس الشيء بقهره، وهو قريب من المعنى الأول

words: كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those before us” refers to the People of the Book, especially the Jews, as the sūra's stories and 7:157 suggest.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالذين من قبلنا هم أهل الكتاب وخاصة اليهود على ما تشير السورة

words: وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea concerns punishment for sins—unbearably hard duties, inflicted torment, or a scourge such as transformation—not an initial impossible duty, which reason excludes.
rows.anchor: ليس هو التكليف الابتدائي بما لا يطاق، إذ قد عرفت أن العقل لا يجوزه أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three pleas progress from specific effect to general source: pardon removes sin's effect or recorded punishment, forgiveness removes and veils its inward state, and mercy is God's gift covering both.
rows.anchor: العفو محو أثر الشيء، والمغفرة ستره، والرحمة معروفة، وأما بحسب المصداق فاعتبار المعاني اللغوية يوجب أن يكون سوق الجمل الثلاث من قبيل التدرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because these three pleas follow the request not to be charged for forgetting or error, they concern sins arising from forgetfulness, error, and similar failings.
rows.anchor: على ما للجميع من السياق والنظم يشعر بأن المراد من العفو والمغفرة والرحمة ما يتعلق بذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested forgiveness is specific to sin through error or forgetfulness, unlike the absolute “Your forgiveness, our Lord” answering the believers' absolute assent; the requests are not redundant.
rows.anchor: فإنه مغفرة مطلقة في مقابلة الإجابة المطلقة على ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “our Lord” four times evokes divine mercy and recalls the speakers' servitude and abasement.
rows.anchor: وقد كرر لفظ الرب في هذه الأدعية أربع مرات لبعث صفة الرحمة بالإيماء والتلويح إلى صفة العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlā means a supporter who takes charge of the supported person's affairs, not just any helper; God is believers' guardian and protector.
rows.anchor: والمولى هو الناصر لكن لا كل ناصر بل الناصر الذي يتولى أمر المنصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer shows that after assent to religion they turn to establishing and spreading it: calling to truth, striving, enjoining right, and uniting peoples to end division, a central purpose of religion.
rows.anchor: وهذا الدعاء منهم يدل على أنهم ما كان لهم بعد السمع والطاعة لأصل الدين هم إلا في إقامته ونشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The petition shows that public calling to religion was the believers' first concern after committing themselves to hear and obey.
rows.anchor: فقولهم أنت مولانا فانصرنا يدل على جعلهم الدعوة العامة في الدين أول ما يسبق إلى أذهانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vow is a person's making obligatory upon himself something that was not obligatory.
rows.anchor: النذر إيجاب الإنسان على نفسه ما ليس بواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥrīr means release from a bond, as in freeing a slave or “releasing” meanings from the mind in writing.
rows.anchor: والتحرير هو الإطلاق عن وثاق ومنه تحرير العبد عن الرقية وتحرير الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqabbul is acceptance with willingness and approval, like accepting a gift or a prayer.
rows.anchor: والتقبل هو القبول عن رغبة ورضى كتقبل الهدية وتقبل الدعاء ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her wording indicates she spoke while pregnant and that Imran was the father; the passage hints he had died, since otherwise she could not independently dedicate the unborn child, as 3:44 also suggests.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أنها إنما قالت هذا القول حينما كانت حاملا وأن حملها كان من عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parent's dedication does not manumit a child; it releases the child from parental guardianship and use for the parents' aims, placing the child under God's authority for worship and service.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن تحرير الأب أو الأم للولد ليس تحريرا عن الرقية وإنما هو تحرير عن قيد الولاية التي للوالدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported custom was to dedicate a child to God for church service and cleaning until puberty, then let the child choose to stay or leave.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل إنهم كانوا يحررون الولد لله فكان الأبوان لا يستعملانه في منافعهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She believed the unborn child was male: her vow is unconditional, and the masculine “dedicated” is not merely agreement with the gender-neutral “what”; otherwise her grief at a girl and the later contrast would be unexplained.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام دلالة على أنها كانت تعتقد أن ما في بطنها ذكر لا إناث حيث إنها تناجي ربها عن جزم وقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her certainty was not a guess based on women's intuition: God's narration does not leave falsehood uncorrected, so her firm claim about the womb had a truthful basis.
rows.anchor: اعتقادها ذلك لم يكن عن جزاف أو اعتمادا على بعض القرائن الحدسية التي تسبق إلى أذهان النسوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the fetus's sex belongs to God's unseen knowledge (13:8; 31:34), and knowledge of the unseen reaches others through revelation (72:26), Mary's certainty about a son must have been revealed.
rows.anchor: فجعل العلم بما في الأرحام من الغيب المختص به تعالى وقال تعالى عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا إلا من ارتضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discovering the child was female, Mary still confidently prayed for her and her descendants' protection, indicating hope for offspring beyond the girl.
rows.anchor: لما تبينت أن الولد أنثى لم تيأس عن ولد ذكر فقالت ثانيا عن جزم وقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “accept from me” is omitted and could be either her vow or the consecrated child; 3:37's “accepted her” suggests she meant acceptance of the child.
rows.anchor: نذرها من حيث إنه عمل صالح أو يكون هو ولدها المحرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the feminine pronoun for what had been in her womb is a concise way of saying she gave birth to it and discovered it was female; her following statement expresses grief, not mere information.
rows.anchor: في وضع الضمير المؤنث موضع ما في بطنها إيجاز لطيف والمعنى فلما وضعت ما في بطنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both parenthetical statements are God's, not the mother's: God knew she had borne a girl and meant to fulfill her hope in a better way.
rows.anchor: جملتان معترضتان وهما جميعا مقولتان له تعالى لا لامرأة عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary surpassed the hoped-for boy: she and Jesus would be a sign to the worlds, with Jesus born without a father, speaking in the cradle, and being God's spirit and word.
rows.anchor: لكن هذه الأنثى ستتم بها كلمة الله وتلد ولدا بغير أب وتجعل هي وابنها آية للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine-first comparison is God's evaluation: if the disappointed mother were speaking, she would say the girl is not like the boy she wanted, rather than the reverse.
rows.anchor: فإن من كان يرجو شيئا شريفا أو مقاما عاليا ثم رزق ما هو أخس منه واردأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in “the male” and “the female,” or at least in the latter, is referential.
rows.anchor: وظهر من ذلك أن اللام في الذكر والأنثى معا أو في الأنثى فقط للعهد

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes attach “the male is not like the female” to the mother's speech and offer explanations for putting “male” first.
rows.anchor: وقد أخذ أكثر المفسرين قوله { وليس الذكر كالأنثى } تتمة قول امرأة عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that majority reading: their explanations for the inverted comparison yield no coherent result.
rows.anchor: وتكلفوا في توجيه تقديم الذكر على الأنثى بما لا يرجع إلى محصل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Mary is said to mean “worshipper” or “servant” in her language.
rows.anchor: معنى مريم في لغتهم العابدة والخادمة على ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having lost hope of a boy dedicated to worship, Mary’s mother named the girl Mary, thereby dedicating her to worship and church service; this amounts to renewing the vow, as 3:37's acceptance indicates.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة أن تقول إني جعلت ما وضعتها محررة لك والدليل على كون هذا القول منها في معنى النذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She seeks God's protection for Mary and her descendants from Satan so their worship and service will match Mary's name and dedication.
rows.anchor: ثم أعاذتها وذريتها بالله من الشيطان الرجيم ليستقيم لها العبادة والخدمة ويطابق اسمها المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her unqualified prayer about Mary's future descendants exceeds ordinary human knowledge; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī infers she knew by revelation that a righteous son promised through Imran would come from Mary's line, so she shifted her dedication to the daughter.
rows.anchor: فليس إلا أنها كانت تعلم أن سترزق من عمران ولدا ذكرا صالحا ثم لما حملت وتوفي عمران لم تشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her good growth means God gave Mary and her descendants guidance, purity, and a life untouched by Satan's whispering and temptation.
rows.anchor: والمراد بإنباتها نباتا حسنا إعطاء الرشد والزكاة لها ولذريتها وإفاضة الحياة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good acceptance and growth correspond to God's choosing and purifying Mary in 3:42; her and Jesus' later distinction fulfills the statement that the male is not like the female.
rows.anchor: وهذان أعني القبول الحسن الراجع إلى الاصطفاء والنبات الحسن الراجع إلى التطهير هما اللذان يشير إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah became Mary's guardian when the lot fell to him after the disputants agreed to draw lots, as 3:44 relates.
rows.anchor: وإنما كفلها بإصابة القرعة حيث اختصموا في تكفلها ثم تراضوا بينهم بالقرعة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Rāghib lists explanations of miḥrāb: a place to combat Satan and desire, a place free of worldly distraction, or a room's front modeled on the mosque's; he favors the last account.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب ومحراب المسجد قيل سمي بذلك لأنه موضع محاربة الشيطان والهوى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify this miḥrāb with the Christian altar or sanctuary, an elevated enclosed chamber at the temple's front; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī traces the Islamic prayer enclosure to this form.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المحراب هنا هو ما يعبر عنه أهل الكتاب بالمذبح وهو مقصورة في مقدم المعبد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported example of Mary's unusual provision is winter fruit appearing in summer and summer fruit in winter.
rows.anchor: كما قيل إنه كان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف وفاكهة الصيف في الشتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “provision” signals unfamiliar food; if it were ordinary food, visitors to the mosque might have brought it, so Mary's answer would not rule out a human source.
rows.anchor: إشعار بكونه رزقا غير معهود كما قيل إنه كان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's naming of Yahya in the annunciation supports that Zechariah asked for a child like Mary; she and Jesus are one sign to the worlds (21:91).
rows.anchor: وتسميته بيحيى وكون التسمية من عند الله سبحانه في بدء ما بشر به زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya parallels Jesus as far as possible, but Jesus precedes him in God's plan and uniquely has the rank of an ulu al-ʿazm messenger with a scripture and law.
rows.anchor: ولعيسى في ذلك كله التقدم التام لأن وجوده كان مقدرا قبل استجابة دعوة زكريا في حق يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī aligns Yahya with Jesus: childhood wisdom, mercy and purity, dutifulness without tyranny, peace at birth, death, and resurrection, and parallel prophetic honors.
rows.anchor: وعده حنانا من لدنه وزكاة وبرا بوالديه غير جبار كما كان عيسى كذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Yahya's name is said to mean “he lives,” and his being named by God and confirming God's word further parallels Jesus.
rows.anchor: وهو بمعنى " يعيش " على ما قيل وجعله مصدقا بكلمة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These parallels answer Zechariah's prayer for righteous offspring and a pleasing successor, a request prompted by what he witnessed of Mary's extraordinary favor.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك استجابة لمسألة زكريا ودعوته حيث سأل ذرية طيبة ووليا رضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An āya is a sign that points to a thing.
rows.anchor: والآية هي العلامة الدالة على الشيء

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One reported view is that Zechariah asked for a sign to know when his wife would become pregnant; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī finds this somewhat distant from the narrative's flow.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه أراد أن يستدل بها على حمل امرأته ويعلم وقت الحمل خلاف بين المفسرين

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: Some exegetes avoid reading the sign as distinguishing a divine angelic message from satanic whispering, arguing that an infallible prophet must recognize the difference and cannot be confused by Satan.
rows.anchor: الذي أوجب تحاشي القوم عن الذهاب إلى أول الوجهين أعني كون سؤال الآية لتمييز أن الخطاب رحماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets' recognition is taught by God rather than independent of him, so there is no problem in Zechariah asking God for a sign to identify the message; only a failure to grant it would raise an issue.
rows.anchor: تعرفهم إنما هو بتعريف الله تعالى لهم لا من قبل أنفسهم واستقلال ذواتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three-day loss of speech supports the reading that the sign would confirm the call's divine source: Satan may afflict prophets' bodies or circumstances, but not their inner selves, from which they are protected.
rows.anchor: فإن الشيطان وإن أمكن أن يمس الأنبياء في أجسامهم أو بتخريب أو إفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign was a three-day inability to speak to people, except by gesture, while remembering and praising God; Satan could not directly control the prophet's tongue, so the sign confirms a divine message.
rows.anchor: هو أنه كان لا يقدر ثلاثه أيام على تكليم أحد ويعتقل لسانه إلا بذكر الله وتسبيحه

words: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah could be reassured that the call was divine yet still wonder how conception was possible; after further reassurance, he asked for a sign to deepen his certainty.
rows.anchor: من الممكن أن يكون قد اطمأنت نفسه على كون النداء رحمانيا من جانب الله ثم يسأل ربه من كيفية الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Calling” often suggests a distant, loud voice but distance is not inherent in the word; the wording and Zechariah's secret call in 19:3 suggest he heard a caller without seeing the angel.
rows.anchor: فإن النداء إنما يكون من بعيد ولذلك كثر إطلاق النداء في مورد الجهر بالقول

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say the sign was a command to stop speaking for three days, devote the time to worship in thanks, gesture if needed, and tell his family after the period; completing this worship would mark the promised gift.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض المفسرين أن المراد من جعله تعالى عدم التكليم آية نهيه عن تكليم الناس ثلاثة أيام والانقطاع فيها إلى ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī finds no textual evidence that Zechariah requested a special act of thanks, that completing it would be the sign, that the wording is a legal prohibition, or that he would wait three days to tell his family.
rows.anchor: وأنت خبير بأنه ليس لما ذكره من مسألته عبادة تكون شكرا للمنحة وانتهائها إلى حصول المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech or saying conveys an intended, complete meaning, whether by one or several sounds or without sound; meaningful sounds and gestures both count as speech.
rows.anchor: إنما يسمى به الصوت لإفادته معنى مقصودا يصح السكوت عليه فما يفاد به ذلك كلام وقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also calls meanings Satan casts into hearts his speech and words.
rows.anchor: والقرآن أيضا يسمي المعاني الملقاة في القلوب من الشيطان كلاما له وقولا منه
